attributes.law_screen: Screened all 12 core-screen laws (gdlmem.py laws --tag core-screen --full 1) before the first edit. claim.law.offsetof-rename-preserves-protected-web: PRIMARY technique used throughout -- kept every base pointer's raw u8*/void* type and spelled displacements as offsetof(Type,field) instead of introducing typed intermediates; this is what let large batches (movesPtr/moveCount: 28 sites; c->hdr descriptor/typeFlags/colCount/patternsPtr/file/radii: 45 sites; Critter position fields: ~30 sites) convert in one shot with zero regressions. claim.law.declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast and claim.law.multifield-alias-defeats-indexed-addressing: applicable and heeded -- never introduced a typed alias/cast on a walked or multi-field-touching base (CritterHitNode-walked `record`/`node`, CritterMove-walked `entry`, damage/sfx-table `sfx` locals all stayed raw u8* with offsetof-computed displacements). claim.law.lwzu-idiom-web-retention and claim.law.pointer-walk-array-index-regression: applicable -- no walked-loop pointer was converted to array-indexed form; CritterInitColnodes/CritterUpdateSkinfx kept the `record`/`base` accumulator pattern intact. claim.law.offsetof-fused-immediate-counter: applied for every walked-pointer + big-literal case (hitnodes/mtx/skinMatrix sub-offsets). claim.law.offsetof-rename-array-member-boundary: informed caution around array-typed struct members (kept CritterHitNode.position and Item-view pos as raw offsetof adds, never `->position[k]`). claim.law.large-fn-batch-fuzzy-can-mask-subfield-regression and claim.law.offsetof-overturns-typed-alias-caps: not applicable this session (no >4000-insn functions touched; no prior typed-alias caps revisited). claim.law.recomputed-index-array-form-safe and claim.law.scalar-read-write-lfsu-mixed-form and claim.law.walked-base-symbol-identity: considered, none of their specific trigger shapes (recomputed-index store, adjacent read+write same field, dual-symbol overlap) were hit.
